description:
Continue the conversation in an interactive message. Partially evaluate roughly the next three useful turns: use what is already known to explain the situation, offer consequential proposals, and prepare the follow-ups each plausible answer would invite. Start with a small decision surface and a grounded contribution; put further useful analysis or proposals inside the relevant branch. Do not repeat a summary as an editable input unless editing it changes the next action. An investigation or an editable proposal is a successful outcome; stop when the next step needs new evidence rather than inventing that evidence or extending an exhaustive questionnaire.

Separate observations from assumptions. Ground recommendations in the conversation or inspected material; mark unknowns and use structured choices for structurable plans and text inputs for editable wording. Recommendations are visible reasons, independent of default selection; leave exploratory choices initially empty. Use markdown/text for substantive analysis, select for mutually exclusive directions and multi for compatible approaches the user may explore together. Prefer stable options {id,label,recommendation?,children?}; put answer-specific continuations in children; each selected multi branch stays visible alongside the others. Prefer reveals for checked or selection-wide continuations, then when for cross-branch interactions. Roughly three turns is a foresight horizon, not a required depth. Inspect repository facts yourself; ask the user about consequential choices, not facts you can retrieve. Defaults are proposals until Submit.

FAILURE CASE: a topic selector followed by "Tell me more" delegates the thinking back to the user. Contribute a hypothesis, tradeoff or proposal at the selected branch instead; when evidence is missing, offer the next investigation.

WORKED EXAMPLE: the following CI timings are fictional supplied evidence, not facts about your repository. Notice the analysis, simultaneously explorable changes, stable identities, unselected recommendations, structured exploration, optional detail and shared follow-ups outside the branches. Transfer that structure rather than copying its assumptions:

Widgets: text, markdown, slider, check, input, select, multi, rank, group, disclosure and linear page. A disclosure {disclosure:"Inspect proposal",elements:[...],open?:boolean} collapses detail visually; closing it does not deselect or omit its child answers. when still hides answers. title is optional; omit redundant headings. Give options decision-relevant descriptions (because is an alias). multi.default accepts an option string or array. Stable options use {id,label,description?/because?,recommendation?,children?}; children belongs only to select/multi. Legacy strings or {value,description?/because?,recommendation?} still work and may mix with stable options if wire values are unique. Defaults, selected() and keyed branches use stable ids or legacy values. Prefer inline children; do not also author a keyed branch for the same option. Shared follow-ups belong outside branches in a group with when: any(selected(...),selected(...)). reveals appears while checked or once a selection exists. Conditions use bare ids, selected(id, value), count(id), any/all, comparisons, && || ! and parentheses; quote values containing a closing parenthesis. Hidden values read as unset even with defaults. References must exist; cycles including ancestor/descendant dependencies are rejected. If pages are needed, every top-level element is a page with Back/Next and one final Submit; page.when can skip steps.

Keep notes enabled. Every select/multi supplies Other (please specify) with free text automatically. Widgets using stable options return _other for that option; if authoring _other explicitly, use that exact label. Notes and unexpected answers can change the problem representation; explicit corrections override conflicting widgets. Ask only what still blocks progress. Use unique ASCII ids; avoid status, button, error, _notes, _labels, _option_labels, _route, __proto__, constructor, prototype and generated <id>_other_text collisions. Legacy option values cannot collide with widget properties; stable ids can, but use inline children for those ids. Repair path-specific validation errors and retry. No page.next, conversation nodes, semantic routing, after_submit or intermediate submission exists.

Opening the tool returns awaiting_input with formId and definition, not a decision. Wait for the user message {"type":"popup_result","formId":"…","submissionId":"…","result":{…}}. Its terminal classic result is {"status":"completed","button":"submit","<id>":<value>,"_labels":{…},"_notes":"…"} or {"status":"cancelled"}. A repeated submissionId is duplicate delivery: do not repeat the action. Cancellation stops this question; do not reopen automatically. There is no backend answer storage.

Interpret the submitted evidence: absent keys were hidden or on unvisited pages; input "" is blank, select null unchosen, multi/rank [] empty, check false unchecked. Select returns a stable id or legacy option text; multi/rank return their wire values in arrays (rank in priority order). _option_labels[fieldId] maps selected stable ids to their displayed labels; legacy-only results remain unchanged; slider returns a number; Other adds <id>_other_text. _labels explains ids and _notes adds instructions. Resume the original task from the actual answer, including corrections, without mistaking the opening acknowledgment or an unsubmitted default for agreement.

elements.markdown: Fictional evidence: installs repeat for four minutes; integration tests take eighteen minutes and share a database; Linux, macOS and Windows are covered. Isolation and release commitments are unverified. Caching looks promising; exploration can clarify the larger tradeoffs before committing to changes.

elements.multi: Which directions should we explore together?

options.label: Cache dependencies
options.recommendation: Repeated downloads make this the clearest low-risk lead.

options.label: Rebuild the cache
options.description: Simple invalidation; first run stays cold.
options.recommendation: Start simple before adding fallback complexity.

options.label: Restore a nearby cache
options.description: Potentially faster; verify stale downloads are harmless.

elements.markdown: Cache the download store by OS, runtime and lockfile hash; retain immutable installs. I’ll inspect the install command before choosing paths, since native rebuilds may need a different intervention.

elements.default: Cache dependency downloads without changing dependency resolution.

options.label: Parallelize integration tests
options.description: Target the longest job; inspect shared state first.

options.label: Understand isolation risks
options.recommendation: Inspect fixtures, database naming and cleanup before promising concurrency.

options.label: Database per worker
options.description: Strong separation; migrations and startup cost multiply.

options.label: Schema per worker
options.description: Cheaper setup; verify code has no database-global assumptions.

options.label: Reconsider platform coverage
options.description: Explore PR cost versus platform-specific confidence.

children.markdown: I’ll inspect native code, filesystem-sensitive tests and support policy before proposing exclusions.

options.label: Compare smaller PR matrices
options.description: Preserve the full release matrix while evaluating representative PR checks.

elements.when: any(selected(changes, cache), selected(changes, parallel), selected(changes, coverage))

elements.select: What should the next conversation establish?

elements.markdown: Benchmark caching and parallelism separately before combining them, so faster installs do not conceal database contention.
